claims.text: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
HfNbTaTiZr can be prepared as a single-phase beta-BCC structure without significant chemical short-range order.
Slower cooling or controlled annealing promotes atomic-scale phase clustering and SRO precipitate formation.
High-temperature sintering or additive-manufacturing processing is applicable to refractory HfNbTaTiZr.
A suitable cooling schedule after high-temperature processing permits formation and retention of SRO precipitates.
The modified alloy will contain nanoscale SRO precipitates embedded in a disordered BCC matrix.
SRO precipitates create local variations in the lattice potential.
SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by SRO precipitates decreases the phonon mean free path.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by SRO precipitates shortens the phonon scattering time.
Shorter phonon mean free paths and scattering times lower lattice thermal conductivity.
An HEA containing engineered SRO precipitates will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than a compositionally identical homogeneous disordered HEA.
Processing that suppresses SRO yields a single-phase, chemically random solid solution.
The chemically random baseline has longer phonon scattering times and higher lattice thermal conductivity than the SRO-containing material.
The predicted reduction in lattice thermal conductivity requires that electronic heat conduction not dominate the total thermal conductivity.
The thermal-conductivity reduction depends on the SRO precipitates having an optimal size and distribution.
Laser-flash analysis can provide the lattice thermal conductivity needed for the proposed comparison.
